newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T plays down Florida fund decision.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T plays down Florida fund decision.

text.p: Tobacco to insurance group B.A.T Industries, owners of U.S. tobacco manufacturer Brown & Williamson, played down a decision by Florida pension fund trustees to order its portfolio managers to sell about $825 million of tobacco stocks from its retirement fund.

"This does not represent a new development there were similar moves last year by other states, although we see it as part of the process of the State of Florida trying to apply pressure on the industry," said a B.A.T spokesman.
Robert Milligan, state Comptroller voted against the divestment saying the move was political, but he was defeated two to one on the three member board of trustees.
In August the state of Florida goes to trial against U.S. cigarette companies, in an effort to recover $1 billion or more in Medicaid costs incurred by Florida from tobacco related illnesses.

Maryland's pension funds have exited tobacco stocks, New York has frozen its tobacco holdings in some state pension funds. Texas has purged one of its state-worker pension accounts of tobacco stock and the large New York State Teachers Retirement Fund is shying away from tobacco companies.
B.A.T shares, traded in London, were 3p lower at 559p.
